title: Director, Events
description:
About Engine

At Engine , we’re transforming business travel into something personalized, rewarding, and simple. For too long, managing travel and spend has been overwhelming and fragmented - we’re here to change that. We believe the future of travel should be seamless and powered by technology that delights customers at every step. That’s why we’re building a platform that brings together corporate travel, a powerful charge card, and modern spend management in one place.

To make this vision real, we’re looking for exceptional, mission-driven people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel.

More than 30,000 companies already rely on Engine to support over 1 million travelers and billions in annual bookings each year. Cash flow positive with rapid growth, we pair exclusive Engine -only rates, industry-leading rewards, and intelligent automation to help businesses save money while delivering world-class personalization and convenience.

Backed by Telescope Partners, Blackstone, and Permira, Engine has been recognized as one of the fastest-growing travel and fintech platforms in North America, with honors including the Deloitte Fast 500 and Built In’s Best Places to Work.

About the Role
Events are where Engine ’s brand becomes a felt experience where decision-makers, supply partners, and customers move from knowing our name to living our ambition. We have a diverse set of product lines and business motions, and we need one leader who can make events a core part of how we reach everyone in Engine ’s orbit.
As Director of Events, you’ll own the entire events portfolio: Tier 1 conferences, decision-maker events, supply partner events, partner events, government programs, and our own first-party events for customers. You’ll lead with our brand, design experiences that match our ambitions, and build the playbooks that make every event a measurable, monetizable engine for growth.
Your Mission
Make Engine impossible to ignore in person. You’ll be obsessed with how we lead with our brand and how we turn rooms into momentum, thinking about scale in ways other companies can’t, and creating in-person moments that punch above their weight across every product line and motion.
What You'll Own

• The full events portfolio. Strategy, calendar, budget, and execution across every event type and every product line by creating a single, coherent program rather than a pile of one-offs.

• Tier 1 conferences. How Engine shows up at the industry’s biggest stages: presence, activations, and moments that earn attention and outshine larger competitors.

• Decision-maker events. Intimate, high-intent experiences (dinners, salons, executive gatherings) designed to move the people who sign the deals.

• Supply & partner events. Programs that deepen relationships with our supply partners and the broader partner ecosystem - reinforcing the Engine -only advantage that sets us apart.

• Government & first-party events. Tailored programs for government audiences and flagship, branded first-party events that bring our customers into the Engine world.

• Brand-led experience design. Ensure every event leads with the Engine brand and delivers an experience that matches our ambitions. Not generic booths and lanyards, but moments people talk about.

• Scale through creativity. Find ways to reach more of the market, in more places, for every dollar. Thinking about footprint, formats, and reach in ways that don’t scale linearly with budget.

Playbooks You'll Build

• Attendee recruitment. Repeatable systems for filling every room with the right people. Targeting, invitation, and conversion motions built in partnership with growth, ABM, and sales.

• Measurement. A rigorous framework for what an event is worth: leading indicators through to lagging outcomes.

• Monetization. Models for sponsorships, supply and partner participation, and other ways events drive revenue outside of cost.

Who You Are

• Extensive experience leading B2B and B2C events

Xcelirate develops technologically-advanced platforms which are accessed by thousands of users every minute! What are we looking for?
You're a Principal-Level Full-Stack Engineer. You haven't just been around the block - you helped decide which blocks were worth building, and which ones should've been bulldozed early.
At this point, programming languages don’t really impress you anymore. You treat them as tools that translate intent into something a compiler or interpreter can run, choosing them pragmatically, discarding them without nostalgia, and never confusing syntax or novelty with actual progress.
You’ve been around long enough to remember when PHP constructors shared their class names, when exceptions were returned instead of thrown, and when Yeoman, Underscore, and CoffeeScript felt like the obvious future. More importantly, you also learned when to stop using those awful, awful, creations.
Despite all that experience, you’ve stayed deeply hands-on, and you’ve never been particularly interested in drifting into management just because that seemed like the default next step. You’re still happiest close to the code.
You bring a distinctly stoic approach to your work. You don’t panic when systems misbehave, you don’t chase drama, and you don’t confuse urgency with importance.
When you join a project, things tend to settle down. Code becomes easier to reason about, systems start to feel calmer, and decisions get clearer. Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp is hiring a Senior Recruiter to lead critical searches across our G&A functions.

These teams shape how Ramp grows, protects the business, and maintains a high bar as we scale. You will own searches from initial scoping through close, partnering directly with leaders across Recruiting, Risk, and other G&A functions. You will be expected to develop real fluency in each area you support, translate ambiguous business needs into clear hiring strategies, and bring an independent point of view on talent.

- Own full-cycle recruiting across Recruiting, Risk, and other G&A functions, from intake and market mapping through offer and close.

- Partner with hiring leaders to define the hiring thesis, calibrate the bar, and translate ambiguous needs into clear search strategies and interview plans.

- Build proactive pipelines through market research, targeted sourcing, referrals, and thoughtful engagement with passive candidates.

- 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including significant ownership of G&A, corporate, or specialized business-function searches.

- A track record of independently leading complex or senior-level searches from initial scoping through accepted offer.

- Strong execution and closing skills, including comfort with AI-enabled recruiting workflows, ATS and funnel discipline, competing offers, and sensitive searches.

- Experience improving interview architecture, scorecards, market maps, or recruiting processes where structure was limited or still being built.

- Experience developing AI-enabled recruiting workflows that were adopted beyond your own individual searches.

title: Senior Product Manager, Fulfillment
description:
About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town - we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

Fulfillment is one of Faire's top long-term strategic bets that fundamentally changes how both brands and retailers do business. You'll play an instrumental role in scaling Faire's fulfillment business from 1% to 20%+ of GMV, working across the full problem space of brand supply, retailer demand, and unit economics to build the products and operational foundations that make Faire the best way for brands to fulfill wholesale and the most flexible, valuable way for retailers to stock their stores.

The product problems you'll tackle are both digital and physical in nature, spanning marketplace dynamics, operational systems, and program economics. You'll partner cross-functionally and with senior fulfillment leads to drive end-to-end execution and strategy on key workstreams touching brands, retailers, and operations.

We're looking for a product manager with deep empathy for how our customers' businesses actually work, relentless execution in ambiguous 0→1 environments, and the instinct to always connect what they're building to why it matters for the broader business.

What you’ll do 

• Brand supply.  Build onboarding, sales enablement, and operational tooling that makes it easier and more compelling for brands to fulfill through Faire, with a deep understanding of what it actually takes for a brand to change how they operate.

• Retailer demand.  Drive 50%+ growth to participating brands through Faire Source by closing the discovery, conversion, and cart experience gaps that hold retailers back from making it their primary way to buy.

• Fulfillment experience.  Build toward 90%+ of Faire-fulfilled orders being perfectly delivered, while identifying the net new levers that make fulfillment a genuine differentiator on both sides of the marketplace.

• Unit economics.  Partner with S&A and operations to generate leverage and halve the cost of fulfillment as we scale, from order batching and 3PL collaboration to brand consolidation.

• Cross-functional execution.  Work in close partnership with engineering, design, operations, GTM, finance, and data science to ship end-to-end - defining success metrics and communicating progress, tradeoffs, and decisions clearly across the org.

Qualifications

• Business empathy . You understand how your customers' businesses actually work, not just their user flows. Fulfillment asks brands and retailers to make fundamental operational changes; you grasp those stakes and can navigate the marketplace tradeoffs when their interests intersect.

• Cross-functional execution . You relentlessly chase down problems across eng, ops, design, analytics, and GTM. You earn trust quickly, lead without authority, and work in lockstep with a fast-moving team.

• Systems thinking . You understand how your work fits into the broader puzzle. You don't build shopping experiences without thinking about unit economics, or build brand tooling without thinking about ops partnership.

• Structured problem solving . You systematically break down hard problems and bring creativity and resourcefulness to finding durable solutions.
